title: add runtime NVTX ranges, microbench counters, and perf dashboard
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: We need better visibility into per-kernel latency, KV-cache hot paths, and continuous-batching behavior to diagnose tail latency and guide kernel selection/quantization tradeoffs. This PR adds NVTX ranges around key runtime regions, a lightweight counter API for microbenching hot paths, a microbench harness to exercise prefix and KV-cache scenarios, and a Grafana dashboard to visualize results.

What this changes: - NVTX instrumentation: add scoped NVTX ranges for scheduler decisions, batching loop, kernel dispatch, KV cache lookup/insert, and attention/flash kernels. Ranges include attributes for request id, model, sequence length, and batch size. - Counter API: small atomic counters exposed from runtime that can be sampled by microbench to compute rates and hit/miss ratios for prefix caching and batching. - Microbench harness: bench_prefix_latency.py to run deterministic traces (prefix-heavy, full-sequence, random lengths) and record NVTX + counters using local CUDA profiling. - Perf dashboard: Grafana JSON with panels for per-range latency histograms, KV-cache hit/miss ratios, batching size distribution, and trend lines for regressions. - CI integration: optional perf-workflow to run the microbench on a small synthetic trace on PR (disabled by default; gated behind perf-run label).

Checklist: - [x] NVTX scoped ranges added to runtime hotpaths - [x] Counter API implemented and documented - [x] Microbench harness + runner + sample traces - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON added - [x] Unit tests for instrumentation macros - [x] Perf CI workflow (opt-in) - [x] Documentation: runtime/INSTRUMENTATION.md and console README

Links: Linear: ENG-4821, ENG-4923; Internal doc: https://linear.redwood.dev/notes/runtime-profiling; Grafana preview: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/runtime/runtime-perf

Notes on behavior: instrumentation is opt-in (enabled by env REDWOOD_RUNTIME_INSTRUMENTATION). When disabled there is zero NVTX/counter overhead. NVTX ranges compile out on non-CUDA builds to avoid runtime dependencies. The counter API uses relaxed atomics and exposes sampling APIs to avoid skewing latencies.

Testing performed: unit tests for macros and counters; end-to-end microbench runs on local GPU workers; CI run included a perf-regression job that initially timed out on the synthetic large trace and was tuned to use a smaller sample and re-run successfully.
commits: 1) Add NVTX macros and scoped ranges to runtime instrumentation layer; 2) Wire NVTX into scheduler, batching loop, kernel dispatch path, KV cache lookup/insert; 3) Implement Counter API and minimal sampling endpoint; 4) Add microbench harness and sample traces; 5) Add Grafana dashboard JSON and README; 6) CI perf workflow and docs.
files_changed: runtime/src/instrumentation/nvtx_instrumentation.cpp: add NVTX ranges for kernel launch, kv-cache ops, batching loop
runtime/include/instrumentation.h: public API for counters, scoped NVTX macros and build-time guards
runtime/src/kv_cache/kv_cache.cpp: add NVTX ranges around lookup/insert and increment counters on hit/miss
runtime/src/scheduler/batching_loop.cpp: add NVTX ranges and sampling hooks for batch formation
tools/microbench/bench_prefix_latency.py: new microbenchmark harness and runner with sampling and NVTX export
observability/dashboards/runtime-perf.json: new Grafana dashboard for NVTX ranges, per-kernel histograms, KV-cache metrics
ci/perf-workflows/bench-ci.yml: opt-in perf job to run microbench on a small synthetic trace
docs/runtime/INSTRUMENTATION.md: usage, env vars, and examples
docs/console/README.md: how to import the runtime perf dashboard
review_comments: Evan Li: Can we avoid allocating strings per request in the NVTX attributes? Suggest preformatting a short label and using id mapping.
Author (Sofia Patel): Good call — switched to a static short label + numeric attrs; updated tests and documentation.
Marcus Nguyen: The KV cache counters look fine, but the sampling API may skew results when called on the hot path. Can we sample at tunable rates?
Author (Sofia Patel): Added env REDWOOD_INSTRUMENTATION_SAMPLE_RATE (default 0.01) and ensured atomic counters are used so the hot path cost is minimal.
Priya Desai: Dashboard looks useful. Please add a panel for 'batch size distribution' and a breakdown by model.
Author (Sofia Patel): Added batch size distribution panel and model label grouping.
Evan Li: CI perf job initially timed out; we should gate the long traces behind a flag.
ci_runs: perf-regression: fail (timeout on large synthetic trace) -> tuned trace size -> rerun -> pass
release_notes: Added NVTX ranges and lightweight counters for runtime profiling; introduced a microbench harness and Grafana dashboard to observe per-kernel and KV-cache performance. Instrumentation is opt-in and off by default.
